gp_wait_7d.title: Waiting time for elective outpatient medical visit (physician) in primary health care exceeds 7 days from assessment of the need for treatment, % appointments kept
gp_wait_7d.title_fi: Perusterveydenhuollon avosairaanhoidon lääkärin kiireettömän käynnin odotusaika yli 7 pv hoidon tarpeen arvioinnista, % toteutuneista käynneistä
gp_wait_7d.organization: Finnish institute for Health and Welfare (THL)
gp_wait_7d.description: The indicator gives the percentage (%) of all patients with a non-urgent physician's appointment in primary health care outpatient care who were not admitted to an appointment within one week.The waiting time is calculated from the first contact made to the completed procedure. The indicator includes Register of Primary Health Care visits (Avohilmo) visits, which contain waiting time monitoring data. Classifications based on the Hilmo -guide (in Finnish): Service form (in Finnish): Outpatient health care (T11) Method of contact (in Finnish): Physical visits (R10-R45) including e-service appointments (R46-R59) Urgency of care: Non-urgent care (E) Type of visit: Medical care Occupation of the recipient: Doctor or comparable

referral_3d.title: Referrals for specialised health care received processed within 3 days, % of referrals received
referral_3d.title_fi: Erikoissairaanhoitoon saapuneet 3 vrk:ssa käsitellyt lähetteet, % saapuneista lähetteistä
referral_3d.organization: Finnish institute for Health and Welfare (THL)
referral_3d.description: The indicator describes the waiting time for the start of the assessment of access to specialized medical care from the date of receipt of the referral to the date of processing the referral. According to the Health Care Act (2010/1326/52§ - 53§), the assessment of the need for treatment in non-urgent care must begin within three weeks of the referral arriving at the hospital of the joint municipal authority or other unit providing specialized medical care. However, the majority of referrals are processed faster than this. A processed referral refers to a referral on which a doctor has taken a position and on the basis of which he has made a plan for further measures. The index describes producer-specific information. As a rule, referrals to hospitals in a wellbeing services county concern residents of the the wellbeing services county in question. The data does not include emergency room referrals or referral information for specialized medical care services provided by primary health care.

wait_6m.title: Patients waiting over 6 months during the year for access to specialised health care per 10 000 inhabitants
wait_6m.title_fi: Erikoissairaanhoitoa yli 6 kk odottaneet vuoden aikana / 10 000 asukasta
wait_6m.organization: Finnish institute for Health and Welfare (THL)
wait_6m.description: The indicator gives the number of patients waiting over 6 months for access to specialised health care per ten thousand inhabitants in a given year. The indicator is calculated as an average of the data reported monthly by the wellbeing services counties. Population proportions are calculated at THL based on the Population Statistics of Statistics Finland. A patient is considered to be waiting for treatment when a physician or another health care professional has, based on an assessment of the need for treatment, made a treatment decision and placed the patient on a waiting list for treatment (the reason for queueing is hospital resources) or booked an appointment in outpatient care for the patient. Patients queuing for treatment include patients who are waiting for an operation, procedure or other treatment. The date of placement in the treatment queue is the date when the patient is placed in the queue for treatment, operation or procedure. The date of placement in the treatment queue should be the same date when the physician has decided on treatment. surv_breast.title: Five-year relative survival rate of breast cancer patients, %
surv_breast.title_fi: Rintasyövän sairastaneiden viiden vuoden suhteellinen elossaololuku, %
surv_breast.description: The indicator represents the five-year relative age-standardised survival rate of breast cancer patients, (0100 percent). The figure indicates the percentage of cancer patients alive five years after cancer diagnosis, compared to the percentage of the population of a similar age in the region surviving during this time. The relative survival rate can be interpreted as an estimate of the likelihood of survival in a situation where the cancer of the patient is the only possible cause of death. This is based on the monitoring of patients diagnosed during the statistical year visible on Sotkanet, and during the nine preceding years, carried out during the statistical year and the four years preceding the statistical year. The regional survival rates have been age-standardised to correspond to the age structure of the patients diagnosed in the entire country during the monitoring years.

travel_barrier.title: Bad travel connections hampered access to care, (%) of persons who used health services (2018-)
travel_barrier.title_fi: Hankalat matkat haitanneet hoidon saantia, (%) terveyspalveluja käyttäneistä (2018-)
travel_barrier.organization: Finnish institute for Health and Welfare (THL)
travel_barrier.description: The indicator shows the percentage of health service users aged 20 or over who felt that bad travel connections at least sometimes hampered access to care. Based on the question: "Have the following factors interfered with you receiving treatment in the past 12 months?: - The place of care was hard to reach. The response options were: 1) always, 2) most of the time, 3) sometimes, 4) never, 5) does not apply to me or the services I have used. The examination includes the respondents choosing option 1), 2) or 3) who had used health services.

smokers.title: Daily smokers (%)
smokers.organization: Finnish institute for Health and Welfare (THL)
smokers.description: The indicator gives the percentage of daily smokers aged 20 and over in the total population of the same age. The respondents were requested to answer the following question about smoking: Do you currently smoke (cigarettes, cigars or pipe)?. The response options were 1) yes daily, 2) occasionally, and 3) not at all. The proportion of those who chose the response option 1 were included in the indicator.

hpv_girls.title: Coverage of HPV-vaccine, girls
hpv_girls.organization: Finnish institute for Health and Welfare (THL)
hpv_girls.description: The indicator shows the share of girls who have been given the HPV vaccinations preventing several different cancers according to the vaccination programme when in primary school age. The share of girls given a total of two doses of the HPV vaccine of girls turning 13 in the year of reporting. The HPV vaccination coverages are assessed and published in autumn. The coverage assessment includes the vaccinations that have been given during the two school years preceding the autumn of reporting. Vaccination data are collected by school year and the collection time is always from August to the end of July the following year.

population.title: Population at year end
population.description: The indicator gives the permanent resident population (males and females combined) of a municipality on the last day of the year. Those who according to the Population Information System are domiciled in Finland at the end of the year belong to the permanent resident population whatever their nationality, as do Finnish nationals temporarily residing abroad.
